column1: # Junctions excluded from the annotated SV table.
# Each row was observed at base-identical coordinates in unrelated patients,
# across five sequencing depths from 8 to 32 hours. Somatic breakpoints do not
# recur to the nucleotide between individuals: repair at a real junction is
# imprecise, so two patients sharing a rearrangement share the intron, not the
# base. Identity to within a few bases is a mapping or reference artefact.
# Recurrence alone is NOT the criterion, and must not become one. Acute
# leukaemia's defining events are recurrent by definition: KMT2A, MECOM and
# NUP98 rearrangements are expected in multiple patients and are findings, not
# noise. What is excluded here is coordinate identity, which is a different
# claim entirely.
# Three of these sit on panel anchor genes — MECOM, RARB and MYC — where the
# anchor rule would otherwise make every artefact reportable. That is the
# reason the list exists.
# A row whose dictionary entry names it, or whose tier is defining, is never
# excluded regardless of what matches here. The override is in
# annotate_al_fusions.py and is not configurable.
# Positions are 1-based, on T2T-CHM13v2.0. TOLERANCE is the window either
# side, in bp, within which a call is treated as the same artefact. Both
# orientations are matched, so a reciprocal mate needs no separate row.
